Patch 0.39.0 (social.go extracted)

  • New package file: server/internal/game/social.go (71 lines) — DefaultSocialStatus, validSocialStatuses, NormalizeSocialStatus, SetPlayerSocialStatus, SetPlayerSocialStatusAutomatic.
  • party.go gains GetAllParties: moved from world.go; world.go reduced from 9 394 → 9 325 lines.

Patch 0.38.4 (Friends list and presence — test coverage)

  • DB integration tests: 17 Go tests covering all six friendship CRUD methods; run against a live Mongo instance when MONGO_URI is set, skip cleanly otherwise.
  • Server helper tests: Pure unit tests for usernameToPlayerID, playerIDToUsername, and buildFriendListPayload; DB-gated handler tests for all five MsgFriend* message cases.
  • SocialUI friends tests: 32 JS tests covering friend list rendering, presence updates, incoming request display, tab switching, badge counts, and all four friend callbacks.
  • UIManager toast tests: 16 JS tests covering online-only firing, disabled toggle, per-user rate limiting, 30-second reset, ARIA attributes, localStorage persistence, and _renderFriendToast DOM output.
  • Regression coverage: Added Go and JS test suites for all 0.38 server, UI, and toast surfaces and the 0.38.4 release state.

Patch 0.38.3 (Friend-online toast)

  • A toast appears when a friend comes online: A brief notification slides in at the bottom of the screen showing "username is now online." so you do not have to poll the Social window.
  • Rate-limited per user: The same friend triggers at most one toast every 30 seconds, so rapid reconnects do not spam the screen.
  • Opt-out persists across sessions: Settings exposes a toggle stored as eidolon.friendOnlineToast in localStorage; defaults to enabled.
  • Accessible markup: The toast element carries role="status" and aria-live="polite" so screen readers announce it without interrupting active interaction.
  • Regression coverage: Added UIManager toast coverage for rate limiting, toggle persistence, DOM output, and the 0.38.3 release state.

Patch 0.38.2 (Friends sub-panel in Social window)

  • Social window gains a Friends tab: The header now shows Online and Friends tabs; the Friends tab lists accepted friends with live online/offline status.
  • Friend actions are in-panel: Each friend entry has Remove and, for online friends, a presence badge; pending incoming requests appear with Accept and Decline buttons.
  • Add Friend input: A text field and button let you send a friend request by username from within the Friends tab.
  • Badge on the tab: An unread count badge on the Friends tab lights up when a new incoming request arrives.
  • Regression coverage: Added SocialUI friends panel coverage for rendering, presence, request handling, and the 0.38.2 release state.

Patch 0.38.1 (Server friend handlers and presence)

  • Five friend message handlers on the server: The server now handles friend_request, friend_accept, friend_decline, friend_remove, and friend_list messages.
  • Push-based online presence: When a player joins or disconnects, the server pushes a friend_presence message to every accepted friend who is currently online.
  • Friend list on connect: The client receives a fresh friend list payload on the first state message so the Friends panel is populated without a manual refresh.
  • Regression coverage: Added server handler and presence helper coverage and the 0.38.1 release state.

Patch 0.38.0 (Friendships database schema)

  • A persistent friendship table is live: The friendships MongoDB collection stores directed relationships with requester_id, addressee_id, and status fields.
  • Mutual-accept model: A request must be accepted before either side sees the other in their friend list; duplicate requests in either direction are blocked at the DB layer.
  • Six CRUD methods: SendFriendRequest, AcceptFriendRequest, DeclineFriendRequest, RemoveFriend, GetFriends, and GetPendingRequests cover the full friendship lifecycle.
  • Regression coverage: Added Go DB schema, indexes, CRUD methods, and the 0.38.0 release state.

Patch 0.37.4 (Social status enforcement and auto-transitions)

  • Busy blocks party invites: The server now rejects party invitations sent to a player whose status is Busy, and the inviter receives a clear explanation.
  • Dungeon entry automatically sets In Run: When your party enters a dungeon, the server sets every member's status to In Run and broadcasts the updated roster — no manual update required.
  • Respawn and Recall automatically restore Available: Returning to the overworld via respawn or recall reverts your status from In Run to Available and triggers a fresh roster broadcast.
  • Busy is respected throughout: If you explicitly chose Busy before entering a dungeon, the server will not override it — on entry or on return.
  • Regression coverage: Added server and client coverage for busy invite blocking, automatic in-run transitions, available revert logic, and the 0.37.4 release state.

Patch 0.37.3 (Proactive social-status broadcast)

  • Social status changes are now visible without reopening the window: When any player changes their status, a fresh roster is pushed to every open Social window within the same server tick.
  • Previously the Social window only refreshed on open: Stale statuses no longer require manually closing and reopening the panel to see updates.
  • Regression coverage: Added server coverage for proactive Social list broadcast and the 0.37.3 release state.

Patch 0.37.2 (Party-member highlight)

  • Party members are visually distinct in the world: A teal ring now appears around the character model of every player in your party — no need to open the Party panel to recognise your group.
  • The ring updates automatically: Joining a party, leaving, or another member disconnecting refreshes the ring for all party members within the same state tick.
  • Existing party and combat flows are unchanged: The ring is a visual overlay; no combat, reward, or party management behavior was modified.
  • Regression coverage: Added client coverage for party ring lifecycle, mesh replacement, and the 0.37.2 release state.

Patch 0.37.1 (Party persistence across disconnects)

  • Party membership now survives a disconnect: Your party ID is stored in the database and rejoined automatically on login if the party is still active when you return.
  • Expired members are cleaned up honestly: If your resume window closes before you reconnect, you are removed from the party at that point rather than silently holding a dead slot.
  • Regression coverage: Added Go unit tests for party rejoin, expired-member cleanup, and the 0.37.1 release state.
